frs_sections.title: Frequency bands and channels
frs_sections.content:
---------------------------------
The 2.4 GHz O-QPSK PHY uses 16 channels numbered 11 through 26, spaced 5 MHz
apart. The channel center frequency Fc (MHz) is:

    Fc = 2405 + 5 * (k - 11)    for k = 11, 12, ..., 26

  Channel 11 = 2405 MHz ... Channel 26 = 2480 MHz.

The 868/915 MHz PHY defines channel 0 (868.3 MHz) and channels 1-10
(906 + 2*(k-1) MHz). The page/channel selection is held in the PHY PIB
attribute phyCurrentChannel and the channel page in phyCurrentPage.

1.2 Modulation and spreading (O-QPSK / DSSS)
--------------------------------------------
The 2.4 GHz PHY employs Offset Quadrature Phase-Shift Keying (O-QPSK) with
half-sine pulse shaping. Each data symbol (4 bits) is mapped to one of 16
nearly orthogonal 32-chip pseudo-random noise (PN) spreading sequences —

frs_sections.title: MAC frame types
frs_sections.content:
-------------------
The MAC sublayer defines four frame types, encoded in the Frame Type subfield
(bits 0-2) of the Frame Control field:

  0b000  Beacon frame          (transmitted by a coordinator)
  0b001  Data frame            (carries an MSDU)
  0b010  Acknowledgement frame (confirms reception of a frame whose AR bit set)
  0b011  MAC command frame     (association, disassociation, data request, etc.)

2.2 MAC General Frame Format (MPDU)
-----------------------------------
  MHR  MAC Header:
       Frame Control (2 octets), Sequence Number (1 octet), Addressing fields
       (Destination PAN ID, Destination Address, Source PAN ID, Source Address),
       Auxiliary Security Header (variable, if Security Enabled)
  MAC Payload (variable)

frs_sections.title: Addressing
frs_sections.content:
--------------
  PAN ID                 : 16-bit Personal Area Network identifier
  Short address          : 16-bit address, allocated on association
  Extended address       : 64-bit IEEE address (EUI-64), globally unique
  Broadcast short address: 0xFFFF
  Unallocated short addr : 0xFFFE
  Addressing modes (2-bit): 0=none, 2=16-bit short, 3=64-bit extended

2.4 Channel access — CSMA-CA
----------------------------
Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance governs medium access.
Two variants:

  Slotted CSMA-CA   : used in beacon-enabled PANs; backoff aligned to the
                      superframe backoff-slot boundaries.
  Unslotted CSMA-CA : used in non-beacon-enabled PANs; free-running backoff.

frs_sections.title: Association / scanning
frs_sections.content:
--------------------------
  Energy Detection (ED) scan  : measure channel energy for PAN start.
  Active scan                 : send Beacon Request, collect beacons.
  Passive scan                : listen for beacons (beacon-enabled).
  Orphan scan                 : relocate a coordinator after loss of sync.
A device joins by issuing an Association request MAC command and receiving a
short address in the Association response.

frs_sections.title: NWK overview
frs_sections.content:
----------------
The Zigbee Network layer (NWK) sits above the 802.15.4 MAC. It is responsible
for joining and leaving a network, applying security to frames, routing frames
to their destination, discovering and maintaining routes, and discovering and
maintaining one-hop neighbours. Zigbee supports star, tree, and mesh
topologies; Zigbee Pro uses mesh routing.

3.2 Zigbee device roles (NWK)
-----------------------------
  Zigbee Coordinator (ZC) : exactly one per network; forms the network,
                            selects the PAN ID and channel, is the Trust Center,
                            allocates the network key; an FFD; address 0x0000.
  Zigbee Router (ZR)      : an FFD that relays packets (extends mesh range),
                            permits other devices to join, and rout…

frs_sections.title: NWK addressing and routing
frs_sections.content:
------------------------------
  Network (short) address : 16-bit, assigned at join time.
  Routing                 : mesh routing based on an AODV-derived (Ad hoc
                            On-demand Distance Vector) route discovery — Route
                            Request (RREQ) / Route Reply (RREP) broadcast/unicast;
                            also tree (Cskip distributed addressing) and source
                            routing for many-to-one (concentrator) flows.
  Neighbor table          : one-hop neighbours and their link costs.
  Routing table           : destination -> next-hop entries with status.
  Broadcast               : network-wide broadcast with passive acknowledgement.

frs_sections.title: NWK frame format
frs_sections.content:
--------------------
  NWK Header: Frame Control (2 octets), Destination Address (16-bit),
              Source Address (16-bit), Radius, Sequence Number,
              optional Destination/Source IEEE address, Multicast control,
              Source Route subframe, optional NWK Auxiliary security header.
  NWK Payload.

================================================================================
PART 4 — APPLICATION SUPPORT SUBLAYER (APS) AND ZDO
================================================================================

4.1 APS (Application Support sublayer)
--------------------------------------
The APS provides the interface between the NWK layer and the application. It
maintains the binding table (links source endpoint/cluster to destination),

frs_sections.title: Security services
frs_sections.content:
----------------------
Zigbee security uses AES-128 (128-bit Advanced Encryption Standard) operated in
CCM* (CCM star) mode, providing data confidentiality (encryption), data
integrity (Message Integrity Code, MIC), and replay protection (frame counter).
CCM* is a minor variation of CCM (Counter with CBC-MAC) that additionally
allows encryption-only and integrity-only operation.

  Cipher           : AES-128 block cipher
  Mode             : CCM* (combined CTR encryption + CBC-MAC authentication)
  MIC length       : 0, 32, 64, or 128 bits (security level dependent)
  Frame counter    : 32-bit, monotonically increasing, anti-replay
  Security levels  : 0x00 (none) .. 0x07 (ENC-MIC-128)

frs_sections.title: Keys and Trust Center
frs_sections.content:
-------------------------
  Network key  : 128-bit symmetric key shared by all devices in the network;
                 used to secure NWK-layer frames; distributed by the Trust
                 Center; supports key rotation (Key sequence number).
  Link key     : 128-bit pairwise key for APS-layer end-to-end security between
                 two devices; trust-center link key or application link key.
  Trust Center : a single device (normally the Zigbee Coordinator) that
                 authenticates joining devices and distributes the network key;
                 manages key establishment.
  Install code : per-device pre-configured secret used to derive a unique
                 trust-center link key during commissioning (Zigbee 3.0).

==================================================…

frs_sections.title: Host / SoC interface
frs_sections.content:
------------------------
The SoC exposes the MAC/NWK/APS via SAP primitives (request/confirm/indication/
response). A typical SoC integrates: the O-QPSK/DSSS radio (RX/TX, ED, CCA, LQI/
RSSI), a MAC engine (CSMA-CA, superframe timer, GTS manager, FCS/CRC-16), an
AES-128-CCM* security engine, and the NWK/APS/ZDO/ZCL firmware. Control and
status are exposed through memory-mapped registers and the SAP message
interface; configuration includes channel, PAN ID, short/extended address,
beacon/superframe order, security keys, and the binding/neighbor/routing tables.

frs_sections.title: External RF pins
frs_sections.content:
--------------------
  RF_P / RF_N  : differential 2.4 GHz RF port to the antenna balun/matching
  RF_BIAS      : RF bias
  VDD_RF, VSS  : RF supply and ground
  XTAL_P/XTAL_N: reference crystal (typically 16/32 MHz) for the synthesizer

-----------------------------------
  aMaxPHYPacketSize        = 127 octets
  aTurnaroundTime          = 12 symbols
  aUnitBackoffPeriod       = 20 symbols
  aBaseSlotDuration        = 60 symbols
  aNumSuperframeSlots      = 16
  aBaseSuperframeDuration  = 960 symbols (60 * 16)
  macMaxCSMABackoffs       = 4
  macMinBE                 = 3
  aMaxBE                   = 5
  macMaxFrameRetries       = 3
  Max GTS per superframe   = 7
  Broadcast short address  = 0xFFFF

protocol_overview.type: Low-rate wireless personal area network (LR-WPAN). IEEE 802.15.4 PHY+MAC carrying the Zigbee NWK/APS/ZDO/ZCL stack; packet-based, CSMA-CA medium access, with an optional beacon-enabled superframe.
protocol_overview.duplex: half-duplex (a single 2.4 GHz transceiver time-multiplexes transmit and receive; the radio turns around within aTurnaroundTime = 12 symbols).
protocol_overview.modulation: O-QPSK with half-sine pulse shaping (2.4 GHz); BPSK at 868/915 MHz.
protocol_overview.spreading: Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS): 32 chips/symbol, 16 PN sequences, 2.0 Mchip/s at 2.4 GHz.
layers: PHY (IEEE 802.15.4): O-QPSK/DSSS radio, ED, CCA, LQI/RSSI
MAC (IEEE 802.15.4): CSMA-CA, superframe/GTS, addressing, FCS CRC-16
NWK (Zigbee): mesh/tree/star routing, network key security
APS (Zigbee): binding, reliable delivery, fragmentation, link keys
ZDO (Zigbee, endpoint 0): device & service discovery, management
protocol_overview.security: AES-128 in CCM* mode (confidentiality + integrity MIC + 32-bit anti-replay frame counter); network key (NWK) + link keys (APS); Trust Center.

compliance_requirements: 2.4 GHz O-QPSK/DSSS PHY, 16 channels (11-26), 250 kbps; SFD = 0xA7; aMaxPHYPacketSize = 127.
CSMA-CA medium access with the specified NB/BE/CW defaults.
Four MAC frame types and the MHR/payload/FCS general frame format.
16-bit PAN ID with 16-bit short and 64-bit extended (EUI-64) addressing.
Beacon-enabled superframe with CAP/CFP and up to seven GTS (if beacon-enabled).
FFD/RFD device classes; PAN Coordinator / Coordinator roles.
Zigbee NWK mesh/tree/star routing; APS binding & reliable delivery; ZDO discovery; ZCL clusters.
AES-128 CCM* security with network key + link key, Trust Center, and 32-bit frame counter.

auto_cited_sections.heading: PHY Protocol Data Unit (PPDU) frame format

functional_requirements.text: The 2.4 GHz PHY SHALL transmit O-QPSK with half-sine pulse shaping over DSSS (32 chips/symbol, 16 PN sequences, 2.0 Mchip/s) on one of 16 channels (channel 11-26, Fc = 2405 + 5*(k-11) MHz), at 250 kbps.

The PHY SHALL provide Energy Detection (ED), Clear Channel Assessment (CCA modes 1/2/3), Link Quality Indication (LQI), and transceiver state control (RX_ON / TX_ON / TRX_OFF) with aTurnaroundTime = 12 symbols.
A PPDU SHALL comprise the SHR (4-octet preamble + 1-octet SFD = 0xA7), the PHR (7-bit Frame Length, PSDU <= aMaxPHYPacketSize = 127 octets), and the PSDU (the MPDU).

The MAC SHALL support four frame types — beacon, data, acknowledgement, and MAC command — with an MHR (Frame Control, Sequence Number, addressing, optional auxiliary security header), MAC payload, and a 2-octet FCS (ITU-T CRC-16).

The MAC SHALL access the channel with CSMA-CA: slotted (beacon-enabled, aligned to backoff slots) or unslotted, using NB / BE / CW with macMaxCSMABackoffs = 4, macMinBE = 3, aMaxBE = 5, and aUnitBackoffPeriod = 20 symbols.

In beacon-enabled mode the PAN coordinator SHALL bound the channel with a 16-slot superframe (Beacon Interval BI = aBaseSuperframeDuration*2^BO; Superframe Duration SD = aBaseSuperframeDuration*2^SO; 0 <= SO <= BO <= 14) divided into a Contention Access Period (CAP) and a Contention Free Period (CFP).

The PAN coordinator MAY allocate up to seven Guaranteed Time Slots (GTS) in the CFP, each one or more contiguous superframe slots, with transmit or receive direction, negotiated via a GTS Request MAC command and advertised in the beacon.
Devices SHALL use a 16-bit PAN ID and both a 16-bit short address (assigned on association) and a 64-bit extended IEEE (EUI-64) address; 0xFFFF is the broadcast short address.
The MAC SHALL distinguish Full-Function Devices (FFD: can be PAN coordinator/coordinator, relay, accept associations) from Reduced-Function Devices (RFD: single-coordinator leaf nodes).

The Zigbee NWK layer SHALL join/leave networks, route frames over star/tree/mesh topologies (AODV-derived route discovery with RREQ/RREP, tree Cskip addressing, and source routing), maintain neighbor and routing tables, and apply the network key.
The APS SHALL provide endpoint/cluster addressing (endpoints 1-240, endpoint 0 = ZDO), a binding table, APS acknowledgements, fragmentation/reassembly, and APS-layer (link-key) security.

The ZDO (endpoint 0) SHALL provide device discovery (NWK_addr_req / IEEE_addr_req), service discovery (Node/Simple descriptor, Active_EP, Match_Desc), binding management (Bind/Unbind), and network management (Mgmt_* requests).

The application framework SHALL use the Zigbee Cluster Library: 16-bit cluster IDs with attributes and commands, the ZCL general command set (Read/Write Attributes, Configure/Report, Default Response, Discover), and profile-scoped endpoints (Simple Descriptor).

Security SHALL use AES-128 in CCM* mode providing confidentiality, a Message Integrity Code (0/32/64/128 bits), and a 32-bit monotonically increasing anti-replay frame counter, with a network key, link keys, a Trust Center, and install-code commissioning.

error_response_conditions: FCS (CRC-16) mismatch — the received frame is discarded (no ACK).
CCA busy across macMaxCSMABackoffs (4) retries — CSMA-CA failure; transmission is aborted.
No acknowledgement for an AR-flagged frame within macAckWaitDuration — retransmit up to macMaxFrameRetries (3), then report failure.
PAN ID conflict — PAN ID conflict notification MAC command and coordinator realignment.
Orphaned device (loss of sync) — orphan notification / orphan scan to relocate the coordinator.
Security MIC verification failure or frame-counter replay — frame rejected by the CCM* engine.
Route discovery failure (no RREP) — NWK route error / status report.
